intro: How dividends are taxed, the tax-free dividend allowance, how your Income Tax band decides the rate, which dividends fall outside tax, and when HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) has to be told.
explanation:
## Part of a person's dividends are tax-free, and the rest is taxed at its own rates

Dividends are the payments a company makes to its shareholders. Any dividend income that falls inside the Personal Allowance is not taxed, and there is also a dividend allowance of {fact:dividend_allowance} a year on top. Tax is due only on dividends above the allowance. Dividends from shares held in an ISA are outside tax altogether.

Dividends have their own tax rates, which differ from the rates on wages and pensions: {fact:dividend_basic_rate} in the basic rate band, {fact:dividend_higher_rate} in the higher rate band and {fact:dividend_additional_rate} in the additional rate band. The rates on earnings are set out on the [Income Tax rates and bands](/uk/tax/income-tax/income-tax-rates-and-bands/) page.

## The band is found by adding dividends to other income, and the rates are the same across the UK

Which rate applies depends on total income. To find the band, dividend income is added to other income, so a single person's dividends can be taxed at more than one rate if they straddle two bands.

Dividend rates apply across the UK, Scotland and Wales included. Welsh and Scottish rates change what is paid on wages and pensions, but not on dividends.

## Dividends have to be reported when tax is due on them

HMRC has to be told every year in which tax is due on dividends. Someone who files a Self Assessment return reports the dividends on it by the usual deadline. Someone who does not file one tells HMRC after the tax year ends on 5 April and before 5 October, either by asking for a change to their tax code, so that the tax is collected from wages or a pension, or by contacting the helpline. Dividend income over £10,000 has to go through Self Assessment, with registration by the same 5 October date. Up to that amount, the tax code or helpline route is open to people outside Self Assessment.

Nothing needs to be reported when dividends stay within the allowance.
